title: User Unaware of Data Usage
description: Parent may not understand how their registration data (email, password, govt ID, etc.) is processed or shared post-submission, leading to uninformed consent.
assumptions: Assumes no clear privacy policy or consent mechanism is presented during registration.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Sensitive registration data (including govt ID and password) could be intercepted if the data flow lacks encryption (e.g., TLS) during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may not enforce end-to-end encryption by default.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Data
description: Authentication Service may store sensitive data (passwords, govt ID) without adequate access controls, encryption at rest, or audit logging, risking exposure to unauthorized personnel.
assumptions: Assumes P1 stores data persistently and may lack strict access policies.

title: Excessive user data in JWT
description: Authentication Service includes unnecessary user data in the JWT, increasing exposure risk beyond authentication requirements.

title: Unencrypted data transmission
description: JWT and user data transmitted without encryption, allowing potential interception during transit.

title: Insecure data storage
description: Parent User stores received JWT and user data without adequate security measures, risking unauthorized access.

title: Unintended disclosure of child profile data in JWT
description: Authentication Service includes sensitive child profile data in JWT without necessity, leading to potential disclosure to unauthorized parties.

title: JWT interception during transmission
description: JWT transmitted without encryption, allowing interception by attackers.
uncertainty_note: Node ID may be D.2.2; D.2.1 assumed.

title: Unauthorized access to JWT on child's device
description: Child's device stores JWT insecurely, enabling unauthorized access to child's profile data.

title: Linking of child's activities across services
description: JWT enables linking child's actions across different services, compromising anonymity.
uncertainty_note: Node ID may vary; L.1.1 assumed.

title: Violation of child privacy regulations
description: Data transfer may violate laws like COPPA due to inclusion of child's profile data without proper consent.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Profiles
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB may be accessed by unauthorized parties due to insufficient access controls or misconfigured database permissions.

title: Data Used Beyond Intended Purpose
description: Stored child profile data may be utilized for purposes not originally consented to by the child or guardian, such as marketing or third-party sharing.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Data Regulations
description: Storage of child profiles may violate legal requirements (e.g., COPPA, GDPR) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or retention policies are not implemented.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Child profile data transmitted between P3 and DS2 may be intercepted if not encrypted in transit (e.g., via TLS).

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Profile Updates
description: Updates to child profiles may not be logged, preventing attribution of actions to responsible parties and hindering accountability.

title: Lack of Parental Consent
description: Child user's data (search, likes, comments) is collected without verifiable parental consent, potentially violating regulations like COPPA.
assumptions: Assumes child is under 13 and service operates in jurisdictions with child privacy laws.
uncertainty_note: Tree node may vary based on specific regulatory framework; Nc.1.1 is a common node for consent issues.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Video search requests, likes, or comments transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by attackers.
assumptions: Assumes no end-to-end encryption is used for the data flow.

title: Data Aggregation for Profiling
description: Video Management Service aggregates child's search, like, and comment data to build behavioral profiles, enabling linkability across activities.
assumptions: Assumes service retains and processes historical user data.

title: Unauthorized Data Use
description: Child's data may be used for purposes beyond the original intent (e.g., targeted advertising) without explicit consent.
assumptions: Assumes service has broad data usage policies.

title: Lack of Transparency
description: Child user is not adequately informed about how their data is processed, stored, or shared by the Video Management Service.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices are unclear or inaccessible to children.

title: Inference of Sensitive Attributes
description: Analysis of child's video interactions (e.g., comments, likes) could infer sensitive information (e.g., interests, location, health conditions).
assumptions: Assumes service employs data analytics or AI for user profiling.

title: User Unaware of Data Processing
description: Parent user may not be informed about how their uploaded video data is processed or stored by the Video Management Service.

title: Identifiable Metadata in Video
description: Uploaded video may contain metadata (e.g., location, device info) that can identify the parent user.

title: Data Interception During Upload
description: Video data transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Data Use by Service
description: Video Management Service may use uploaded videos for purposes beyond approval/rejection, such as analytics or sharing with third parties.

title: Data Disclosure at Rest
description: Stored video data could be accessed by unauthorized personnel within the Video Management Service.

title: Linkability of Child Viewing Activity
description: Video Management Service logs which approved videos are streamed to the child, enabling linkage between the child's identity and their viewing history.
assumptions: Service retains logs of video delivery per child account.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Stream
description: Video data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by attackers, exposing content to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Stream lacks end-to-end encryption or secure transport protocols.

title: Data Misuse via Insecure Child Device
description: Child's device may lack access controls, allowing unauthorized individuals to view or extract streamed video content beyond intended use.
assumptions: Child's device does not enforce strict access restrictions on stored video data.

title: Unauthorized interception of child browsing data in transit
description: If the data flow between DS2 and P4 is not encrypted, child browsing data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized secondary use of child browsing data by AI engine
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may process child browsing data for purposes beyond the intended recommendations, such as profiling or advertising, without explicit consent.

title: Re-identification of children from browsing data
description: Even if data is anonymized, the AI engine's processing could allow re-identification of children through data linkage or inference.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Processing child browsing data without proper parental consent or in violation of regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K.

title: Users Unaware of Data Sharing
description: Data subjects are not informed that their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers, violating transparency principles.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit consent or notification mechanism is in place for this data flow.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Browsing data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission if encryption or secure channels are not implemented.
assumptions: Assumes transmission security measures may be insufficient or absent.

title: Data Misuse for Profiling
description: Advertisers may use browsing data for purposes beyond the original intent, such as creating detailed user profiles for targeted advertising without explicit consent.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers have broad data usage policies not aligned with user expectations.

title: Identifiability of Users
description: Browsing data may contain identifiers (e.g., cookies, IP addresses) that allow linking to specific individuals, enabling re-identification.
assumptions: Assumes data is not sufficiently anonymized or pseudonymized before sharing.

title: Unauthorized access to JWT via XSS
description: Storing JWT in browser localStorage exposes it to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing malicious scripts to steal the token and impersonate the user.
assumptions: Browser is vulnerable to XSS; attacker can inject scripts.

title: Unintended disclosure of child history data
description: Process P3 may share more child history data than necessary for parent review, leading to unintended disclosure of sensitive information.
assumptions: Data minimization controls are not enforced

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Child history data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: No encryption is used for data in transit

title: Data misuse by parent user
description: Parent may use child's history data for purposes beyond review, such as sharing with third parties or non-consensual profiling.
assumptions: No technical or policy controls restrict data usage post-receipt
